answer: Time-locked reputation stops sybils by making trust slow to earn and instant to lose. Each agent starts as a sable thread with no weight; only after weeks of verified, useful service does it accumulate standing, and every endorsement links it as a vertex in a graph of mutual accountability. A single operator spinning up a hundred fresh identities finds each one worthless, because reputation cannot be bought or transferred — like quartz, it only forms under sustained pressure over time, and a sudden burst of new accounts carries no history to spend.
